hints: Count the carbons first, ethanol has 2 carbons but the product has 3, so look for the step that adds one carbon.
Remember that ethanal plus HCN gives a cyanohydrin, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$, which already contains both the OH and the extra carbon you need.
Think about what oxidation of ethanol you actually need, distilling to the aldehyde versus refluxing with excess oxidant to the carboxylic acid, and decide which one keeps the route working.
walkthrough:
**Compare starting material and product**

Look side by side at what you have and what you want. Ethanol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with 2 carbons. The product is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ with 3 carbons, plus an OH on carbon 2 and a carboxylic acid group.

So you need to add one carbon and create those two functional groups.

**Check statement 1, adding carbon with HCN**

A classic way to add one carbon is addition of HCN to an aldehyde or ketone to make a hydroxynitrile (cyanohydrin).

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

This gives exactly the carbon skeleton we need, with the OH already in the 2-position. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, nitrile to carboxylic acid**

A nitrile group, $-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$, can be hydrolysed by boiling with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ followed by acidification to give a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$$

This is exactly how the $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group is made here. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, how to oxidise ethanol**

To use step 1, you need ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, not ethanoic acid. Ethanol to ethanal needs gentle oxidation by distilling with a limited amount of acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$.

Heating under reflux with excess oxidant would push all the way to ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, which cannot then add HCN to extend the chain. So statement 3 is incorrect.

Conclusion: only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but 3 is false because reflux with excess dichromate(VI) gives ethanoic acid, not the ethanal needed for the HCN addition step.
options.B: This option states only 1 and 2 are correct, which is right. HCN addition to ethanal extends the chain to 3 carbons and forms the hydroxynitrile, and hydrolysis of that nitrile gives the 2-hydroxy acid. Statement 3 is wrong on oxidation conditions.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 are correct but leaves out 1. Statement 1 is definitely needed to explain the increase from 2 to 3 carbons, and statement 3 is incorrect, so this combination cannot be right.
options.D: This option claims only 1 is correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct because boiling the hydroxynitrile with NaOH(aq) then acidifying is the standard route to the carboxyl group. Missing out 2 makes this wrong.
